message.content:
### Tenant Rights in Texas (as of 2024) | Area | Key Rights | How to Exercise Them | |------|------------|----------------------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlord may charge up to **one month’s rent** for a furnished unit and **two months’ rent** for an unfurnished unit.
• Must be returned within **30 days** after lease ends, minus any lawful deductions. | • Keep a copy of the lease and any receipts for repairs.
• Request a written itemized statement of deductions if you disagree. | | **Habitability** | • Landlord must keep the premises in a safe, sanitary condition (plumbing, heating, electrical, etc.).
• Must comply with all building, housing, and health codes. | • Report problems in writing (email or letter).
• If unresolved, you may file a complaint with the Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs (TDHCA) or local code enforcement. | | **Rent Payment & Late Fees** | • Rent is due on the date specified in the lease.
• Landlord may charge a late fee only if it’s stated in the lease and is reasonable (usually not more than 5% of the monthly rent). | • Pay on time or negotiate a payment plan if needed.
• Keep records of all payments. | | **Lease Termination** | • Either party may terminate a month‑to‑month lease with **30 days’ written notice**.
• For fixed‑term leases, the landlord must give notice before the lease expires if they intend to increase rent or change terms. | • Provide written notice (email or letter) and keep a copy. | | **Rent Increase** | • Landlords can raise rent at the end of a fixed‑term lease or with proper notice for month‑to‑month leases (usually 30 days).
• No statutory cap on rent increases. | • Review the lease for any rent‑increase clauses.
• Negotiate or seek mediation if you feel the increase is unreasonable. | | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | • You have the right to live without unreasonable interference from the landlord or other tenants. | • Report disturbances or harassment to the landlord in writing. | | **Privacy** | • Landlord must give **reasonable notice** (usually 24–48 hours) before entering the unit, except in emergencies. | • Keep a log of any entries and verify that the notice was given. | | **Discrimination** | • Landlords cannot discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, or source of income (e.g., Section 8). | • File a complaint with the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) or TDHCA if you suspect discrimination. | | **Repair and Deduct** | • If the landlord fails to repair a major issue, you may repair it yourself and deduct the cost from rent, but only after giving written notice and allowing a reasonable period for repair. | • Document the problem, send a written notice, keep receipts, and calculate the deduction carefully. | | **Eviction Process** | • Landlord must follow the Texas eviction procedure: serve a **Notice to Pay Rent or Quit** (30 days) or a **Notice to Vacate** (30 days for nonpayment or lease violation).
• Eviction must be filed in court; the landlord cannot forcibly remove you. | • Respond promptly to notices.
• Attend court hearings and bring evidence of compliance. | | **Legal Assistance** | • Free or low‑cost legal aid is available through local legal aid societies, law school clinics, and the Texas Legal Services Center. | • Contact your local legal aid office for representation or advice. | #### Quick Tips for Protecting Your Rights 1. **Read the Lease Carefully** – All obligations and rights are spelled out there. 2. **Keep Written Records** – Emails, texts, and written notices are your best evidence. 3. **Know the Timeline** – Notice periods and deadlines are strict; missing them can cost you. 4. **Seek Mediation Early** – Many disputes can be resolved through mediation before going to court. 5. **Know Your Local Ordinances** – Some cities (e.g., Austin, Dallas) have additional tenant protections beyond state law. --- If you have a specific situation (e.g., a dispute over a security deposit, a repair issue, or a potential eviction), let me know and I can give more tailored guidance or help draft a letter to your landlord.
message.reasoning: The user asks: "What are my rights as a tenant in the state of Texas?" They want information about tenant rights. We can provide general info. There's no request for generating a contract. So we don't need to call the function. Just answer.
